definitions.explanation: A fixed expression whose meaning cannot be fully understood from the individual words alone. Used as a linguistic term when discussing language and grammar.

examples.japanese: この{慣用語|かんようご}の{意味|いみ}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me the meaning of this idiom.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}には{体|からだ}に{関|かん}する{慣用語|かんようご}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many body-related idioms in Japanese.

examples.japanese: {慣用語|かんようご}を{正|ただ}しく{使|つか}えるようになると、{日本語|にほんご}がより{自然|しぜん}に{聞|き}こえる。
examples.english: Once you can use idioms correctly, your Japanese will sound more natural.

notes:
A linguistic term for fixed expressions whose meaning goes beyond the literal words. Japanese is particularly rich in body-part idioms ({体|からだ}の{慣用語|かんようご}), such as {目|め}が{高|たか}い (to have a good eye), {手|て}を{焼|や}く (to have difficulty with), and {腹|はら}が{立|た}つ (to get angry).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {慣用語|かんようご}を{覚|おぼ}える: to learn idioms
- {慣用語|かんようご}の{意味|いみ}: meaning of an idiom
- {体|からだ}の{慣用語|かんようご}: body-part idioms
- {慣用語|かんようご}{辞典|じてん}: idiom dictionary

RELATED WORDS:
- {慣用句|かんようく}: idiomatic phrase — often used interchangeably, but {慣用句|かんようく} specifically refers to phrasal units, while {慣用語|かんようご} can include single idiomatic words
- {諺|ことわざ}: proverb — a complete sentence expressing traditional wisdom, not the same as an idiom
- {四字熟語|よじじゅくご}: four-character compound — a specific class of set expressions using exactly four kanji
